answer: Each identity registers one controllable 5 kW load, a cedar drying kiln whose exhaust plume carries a pigment tracer, with a grid demand-response program. At random stress events the operator orders curtailment within 10 minutes; the utility meter and plume sensor must both show the drop for 30 minutes, checked against the enrolment record, and a missed event revokes the slot. One load cannot curtail twice, so 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 real 5 kW loads, 5 MW total, about $900 per controller ($900,000) plus lost drying work; trade-off: districts with few stress events verify slowly.
